title: Go-Time Lane Prioritizer and KPI Watchlist
body:
Purpose
This is a lightweight, tactical doc to help product-ops make rapid go/no-go decisions when multiple launch lanes (canary, staged, full) are competing for the same support and infra capacity. Focus: prioritize lanes, list the minimal KPI watchlist per lane, and define concrete contingency triggers and immediate actions (20–60 minute response steps).

Who should use this
- Product Ops lead (owner)
- Release engineer on-call
- SRE shift lead
- Customer impact liaison (CS)
- Observability engineer (for dashboard ownership)

Quick summary of intent
We split launch into three "lanes": green (low risk / high concurrency feature-complete), amber (limited users, feature gated), red (enterprise/beta / high touch). This doc maps each lane to a prioritized KPI watchlist and then defines hard thresholds that trigger specific runbook steps. The goal is to reduce subjective judgment in the first 60 minutes of an incident during rollout.

Active lanes (current release candidate)
- Lane: green-lane (self-serve)
  - Target cohort: 50K monthly active tokens (first 24 hours)
  - Traffic pattern: full API (hosted) + SDK calls
  - Primary owner: Maya Patel
  - Secondary: Ethan Chen

- Lane: amber-lane (platform partners)
  - Target cohort: 5–10 pilot customers (session-based)
  - Traffic pattern: sustained long-context sessions
  - Primary owner: Ravi Iyer
  - Secondary: Sofia Alvarez

- Lane: red-lane (enterprise dedicates)
  - Target cohort: single customer staged traffic, high latency sensitivity
  - Traffic pattern: bursty, high throughput windows
  - Primary owner: Sofia Alvarez
  - Secondary: SRE on-call

Core KPI watchlist (per-lane minimal set)
- API success rate (2xx / total) — 1m, 5m, 1h windows
- Per-request p95 latency (inference end-to-end) — 1m, 5m windows
- Token throughput (tokens/sec per model pool) — 1m aggregated
- Queue length / backlog (requests waiting for GPU scheduling) — 15s snapshot
- Error class breakdown (503, 429, 5xx, model OOM) — rolling 30m
- Cost anomaly delta (expected vs observed $/token) — hourly
- Customer-visible failures (support tickets tagged "release-impact") — realtime

Prioritization rules (how to interpret conflicts)
- Rule 1: If green lane exceeds thresholds, pause green traffic before amber or red (green has lowest SLAs).
- Rule 2: Amber has leniency for p95 latency bursts for first 6h if success rate holds >98% and backlog < 12s.
- Rule 3: Red lane (enterprise) gets automated fallback to pinned older model variant first; if that fails, throttle enterprise routing to 30% of baseline and notify account team.

Thresholds -> Immediate actions (first 20 minutes)
- API success rate < 98% for 5m window (any lane):
  - Action A1 (0–5m): Notify SRE via #ops-pager and create incident in PagerDuty. Post initial status in our release Slack channel with lane tag.
  - Action A2 (5–15m): Roll traffic to model-variant-fallback for that lane (automated switch). If automated switch fails, pause lane traffic at the load-balancer routing layer.
  - Action A3 (15–60m): Run triage checklist (see below) and escalate to on-call infra lead.

- p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for 1m window AND backlog rising > 30s:
  - Action L1 (0–10m): Enable smaller batch sizes (runtime config toggle) for the impacted model pool. Notify serving-runtime channel.
  - Action L2 (10–30m): If latency continues, route to a cheaper/older quantized variant for non-enterprise lanes.

- Queue/backlog > 60s (or > 3x baseline)
  - Action Q1: Throttle incoming traffic to lane by 40% via rate-limit policy.
  - Action Q2: If backlog persists after throttle, scale up dedicated capacity (if dedicated plan) or divert to fallback region. Contact infra lead to confirm burst capacity.

Triage checklist (first 60 min, shorthand)
- Check observability: dashboards linked below (errors by code, model metrics, infra GPU utilization).
- Confirm scope: which model/variant, which region, which customer cohort.
- Reproduce: run quick-repro script (ops/repro/run-smoke.sh) against replayed sample payload.
- Configs: verify batch size, KV cache settings, quantization flags.
- Recent changes: check last 3 deploys and any config flips in the last 6 hours.
- Rollback: prepare a one-click rollback artifact and verify rollback plan with infra.

Dashboards and quick links (owner => dashboard)
- Global release watch: dashboards/release-watch (owner: Observability team)
- Model pool health: dashboards/model-pools (owner: Serving runtime)
- Customer impact feed: dashboards/support-signal (owner: CS)

Contingency lane-specific sequences (30–120 minutes)
- Green: pause -> route to cached responses for common prefixes -> resume at 10% if stable.
- Amber: switch to partner-fallback endpoint -> throttle to 50% -> re-run smoke with partner subset.
- Red: immediate switch to pinned model variant -> notify account manager -> escalate to executive ops if >30 min degradation.

Operational runbook snippets (copyable)
- Pause lane traffic (grafana link): run-cmd: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ops/route/pause -d '{"lane":"green-lane"}'
- Switch model variant: run-cmd: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ops/model/switch -d '{"pool":"nvidia-a100-01","variant":"v1.3-quant"}'
- Throttle policy: run-cmd: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ops/ratelimit -d '{"lane":"amber-lane","pct":50}'

Notes-to-self / open questions
- Q1: Do we have automated detection for quantization quality regressions tied to a threshold? (Ravi owning investigation)
- Q2: Confirm whether cost-anomaly alert can be trained to ignore expected token spikes from partner integrations (Ethan).
- TODO: add a small spreadsheet mapping model variants to degrade/rollback side-effects (Maya).

Pre-launch checklist (last 48–2 hours)
- [ ] Confirm canary dataset and smoke scripts exist and are run on nightly build.
- [ ] Validate alerting channels include on-call pager, #release-ops, and partner slack for amber lanes.
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler policy is set and burst credits are sufficient for 6h window.
- [ ] Verify runbook links are live and one-click actions tested in staging.

Post-launch immediate (0–24h)
- Continuous observation 24/7 for first 12 hours; daily summary at 24h.
- Hand-off notes to on-call SRE with explicit items: unresolved signals, any manual mitigations used, customer tickets opened.
- Collect any false-positive alarms and tune thresholds.

Metrics report template (for first 72 hours)
- Field: baseline vs actual (numeric)
- Success rate: baseline 99.5% -> actual X%
- p95 latency: baseline 320ms -> actual Yms
- Token throughput: baseline 120k tokens/hr -> actual Z
- Incident count: baseline 0 -> actual N (with short narrative per incident)

Meeting cadence during rollout
- T-minus 2h: dry-run sync (15m) with owners of each lane.
- T-minus 15m: pre-release check-in (10m) to confirm smoke results.
- Launch +0m to +2h: 15m standups in #release-ops.
- Launch +2h to +24h: hourly async updates, 1 standup at +6h and +12h.

Appendix: quick glossary
- lane: a traffic partition tied to routing policies and SLAs.
- model-variant-fallback: a conservatively quantized or earlier model used when the primary model shows regressions.
- backlog: requests queued waiting for GPU scheduling or runtime batching.

Bottom line
This doc is meant to be a concise, actionable artifact we can staple to a release note and hand to an on-call person. If something is unclear, call out the specific item under "Notes-to-self" and assign an owner. The aim is to reduce ambiguity in the first hour of incidents and accelerate safe progression between lanes.
